name: Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test–Consumption (AUDIT-C)

citations.text: Bush K, Kivlahan DR, McDonell MB, Fihn SD, Bradley KA. The AUDIT alcohol consumption questions (AUDIT-C): an effective brief screening test for problem drinking. Arch Intern Med. 1998;158(16):1789-1795.
Bradley KA, DeBenedetti AF, Volk RJ, Williams EC, Frank D, Kivlahan DR. AUDIT-C as a brief screen for alcohol misuse in primary care. Alcohol Clin Exp Res. 2007;31(7):1208-1217.

validated_population: Adults in primary care (VA general medical clinics). Self-administered.
license_note: AUDIT-C questions are the first three items of the WHO AUDIT, which is freely available. Item wording is used verbatim.

red_flags.question: After cutting down or stopping drinking, do you have shaking, heavy sweating, seeing or hearing things that are not there, or have you had a seizure?
red_flags.help: These are signs of alcohol withdrawal, which can be dangerous.

items.question: What was your sex assigned at birth?
items.help: The positive-screen cut-point differs by sex in the validation studies. If you choose "Another answer", the lower (more sensitive) cut-point is used.

options.label: Another answer / prefer not to say

items.question: How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?
items.help: One drink = 12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, or 1.5 oz liquor.

items.question: How many standard drinks containing alcohol do you have on a typical day?
items.help: One drink = 12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, or 1.5 oz liquor.
items.trace_label: Q2 Drinks on a typical day

items.question: How often do you have six or more drinks on one occasion?
items.help: One occasion means one sitting, party, or evening.
items.trace_label: Q3 Six or more drinks at once

scoring.threshold_text: Positive screen: 4 or more for men; 3 or more for women (and for "another answer"). 8 to 12 suggests severe alcohol misuse.

negative.label: Negative alcohol screen
negative.interpretation: Your score is below the cut-point for alcohol misuse.
negative.recommendation: No action needed. U.S. guidelines advise no more than 2 drinks a day for men and 1 for women, or not drinking.

care.within: No visit needed for alcohol use
ed_redirect: Signs of withdrawal (shaking, seeing things, seizure): go to the emergency department

positive.label: Positive alcohol screen
positive.interpretation: Your score is at or above the cut-point for possible unhealthy alcohol use.
positive.recommendation: Book a primary care visit to talk about drinking and ways to cut down.

care.where_detail: Primary care clinic. Free, confidential help: SAMHSA National Helpline 1-800-662-4357 (24 hours).
ed_redirect: Signs of withdrawal (shaking, seeing things, seizure): go to the emergency department
self_care: If you drink heavily every day, do not stop suddenly without medical advice; withdrawal can be dangerous.

high.label: High alcohol screen (8 to 12)
high.interpretation: Scores of 8 to 12 suggest severe alcohol misuse and a higher chance of alcohol use disorder.
high.recommendation: Book a primary care visit within 1 week. Do not stop drinking suddenly without medical advice if you drink every day.

care.where_detail: Primary care clinic or addiction medicine. Free, confidential help: SAMHSA National Helpline 1-800-662-4357 (24 hours).
ed_redirect: Signs of withdrawal (shaking, seeing things, seizure): go to the emergency department
self_care: If you drink heavily every day, do not stop suddenly without medical advice; withdrawal can be dangerous.
